notes.title: Patch 1.0.6.10 — Keybinding Support & Mod Support Enhancements
notes.content:
This patch introduces a common feature that I had previously missed: keybinding. Although it may seem like a small addition, a lot of underlying code was refactored and changed, so new bugs may appear. Please report any you encounter.

Another noticeable change is the addition of new entities to support mods. Now it’s possible to tweak or create character features such as buffs/debuffs, perks, and skills. Custom research can also be created. It is now possible to design your own items with unique skills or perks and integrate them smoothly into the game.

Thank you for your continued feedback and support — it really helps improve the game!

notes.title: Patch 1.0.6.8 – Armor Dyeing
notes.content:
[p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45205026/07095f9145ac1a9a3fb83172ccc3387ff8e1016a.png"][/img] 1) This patch introduces the ability to [b]dye armor[/b], making it easier to identify characters on the battlefield or distinguish workers by type in your castle. Existing characters will start without a specified color, but it can be changed in the inventory screen. New companions will be assigned a randomly generated color, which can also be customized.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45205026/82b41d8724f50c2dac5d5a3c45967631166924c3.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]2) Another important change in this patch: the [b]default middle mouse action has been changed[/b] to camera rotation, while double-clicking the middle mouse button now controls camera movement. notes.title: Patch 1.0.6.7 – Settlement Raids
notes.content:
[p]This patch introduces a new type of battle: [b]Settlement Raids[/b]. To attack villages, you only need a hostile reputation with faction, but raiding towns requires a specific item additionally. Village raids are designed for mid-game difficulty and primarily focused on increasing reputation, while town raids are end-game encounters with valuable rewards.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45205026/e27ef8cf232a74871c86886330e1a6c446e3a863.png"][/img][/p][p]
I’ve also added a [b]Level-Up History[/b] feature. You’ll now see a new button in the UI that displays all your choices for a character (except attributes).

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45205026/f58d80cd80822abbaba6eef271bfc2e5bdeedb57.png"][/img][/p][p][b]
[/b]An issue with [b]Enhanced Auras was fixed[/b]. They were mistakenly flagged as removable after battle, causing them to disappear after the next fight. Unfortunately, there is no way to restore them, so a respec is required if you selected an Enhanced Aura for a character. Newly chosen Enhanced Auras should now work as expected.
[/p][p]I’ve also fixed and implemented various small improvements mentioned recently.
[/p][p]Thank you for your support, and please accept my apologies ))[/p]

notes.title: Patch 1.0.6.4 – Vulkan Support
notes.content:
I’ve added Vulkan as an optional renderer in this update (DX12 is still default). While it may deliver slightly lower performance compared to DirectX 12 (on modern PCs the difference should be minimal), Vulkan offers much greater stability.

How to enable Vulkan:

[list]
[*] Go to your Steam Library.
[*] Find Shards of the Realm, then click Properties.
[*] Under the General tab, locate Launch Options.
[*] Add:  -vulkan
[/list]

To switch back to DirectX 12, simply remove the launch option.

Thank you for playing and supporting the game! Your feedback helps us make the game better with every update.

notes.title: Patch 1.0.3 Improvements
notes.content: [p]This patch addresses various issues identified by our growing community, introducing important changes and additions to enhance gameplay. It includes two major features: improved movement controls in proximity to enemies and enhancements to weapon mastery functionality.[/p][p]Previously, weapon mastery simply unlocked access to weapons of the corresponding subclass. With this patch, players can now acquire subclass-specific support skills after picking up weapon mastery. For instance, a Berserker can first acquire Sword and Shield Mastery and later unlock the Taunt skill—something that wasn't possible before. This change introduces flexibility and significantly increases the variety of interesting builds available.[/p][p][b]List of Changes:[/b][/p][list][*][p]Movement improvements for melee characters: Reaching enemies is now much easier as the cursor no longer disappears, and the closest viable location is automatically selected. Players still need to manually adjust for optimal positioning, but it's significantly more intuitive.[/p][/*][*][p]Reworked weapon mastery features: Players can now access subclass-specific support skills after choosing weapon mastery.[/p][/*][*][p]Updated textures for Tier 1 (T1) dungeons.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue in the Proficiency Hall where the wrong character name was displayed upon completion.[/p][/*][*][p]Added translations to reflect changes introduced in previous patches.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue causing incorrect skill range display when characters stood on complex terrain.[/p][/*][*][p]"Mad Two-Handed Spin" ability now additionally applies a bleeding effect.[/p][/*][*][p]Save file overwrites now require confirmation to prevent accidental loss of data.[/p][/*][/list][p]Thank you for supporting and helping us improve the game! Enjoy the new changes and expanded build options.[/p]

notes.title: Patch 1.0.2.0 Balance Update
notes.content:
After release, I watched some new videos and noticed where players seem to struggle the most. This patch is aimed at slightly simplifying the early game and improving clarity in tooltips.

Here’s the list of changes:

[list]
[*] Reduced the speed of early-game enemy parties. This change will make traveling easier in the early game and allow players to avoid some combats. It will take effect approximately one in-game week after parties are refreshed.
[*] Lowered HP of starting enemies.
[*] Decreased the cost of hiring new companions by 10 (this change will apply when available companions are refreshed or in a new game).
[*] Reduced the MP cost of Taunt and added one additional usage per turn.
[*] Increased ammo for Fire Staff, Light Priest Staff, and Bow at higher tiers (this won't affect starting equipment).
[*] Added a description to the crouch button.
[*] Added a tooltip when hovering over gold in settlements to display current income and expenses.
[*] Added a research tooltip description (currently only in English; other translations will be updated within a couple of days).
[*] Reduced the cost of some starting research projects.
[/list]

Thank you for your feedback and support! It’s always a huge help in improving the game and making it more enjoyable for everyone.

notes.title: Patch 0.10.4.0 – Bug Fixes and Balance Changes
notes.content:
As I prepare for the upcoming release in a couple of weeks, I continue working on improving game quality and fixing remaining bugs. 

Here’s what’s changed in this patch:

[list]
[*] Since localization assets are still broken on the UE side, I’ve implemented a custom solution — voicelines should now work as expected.
[*] Fixed the post-battle screen to correctly display all 9 party members.
[*] Rifts and sieges now grant more reputation if the battle takes place on a faction's territory (×2.5 and ×4 respectively).
[*] Increased the rotation range of the battle camera, allowing it to get closer to the ground.
[*] Slowed down the rate at which party members gain proficiency.
[*] Fixed a bug where human towns could hire units of any race.
[*] Implemented diminishing returns for building multiple laboratories. The second lab is still a good option, but no longer overpowered.
[/list]

Thank you for your continued support!

notes.title: Patch 0.10.3.0 – Global Map Graphic Improvements
notes.content:
[p]As the game nears release and development is completed, I finally had some free time to address things I previously couldn’t.[/p][p]This update [b]improves the global map[/b], making it feel more alive and less flat than before. Due to changes in terrain, there’s a chance that in [i]this patch only[/i] a party might fall beneath the ground on load. I’ve tried to prevent this scenario, but it may still occur in rare cases.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45205026/30700cd28c539bda7bac7ff3526c2e8deea16f11.png"][/img]
[/p][p]Another noticeable change: I’ve added a tier filter to the production screen, which should help with getting started on crafting.[/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45205026/253b1b88dabaa2a412d8ea4f5711c540072239fd.png"][/img]

Due to migration to Unreal Engine 5.6, global map borders were broken and didn’t appear at the beginning of battles. This has been fixed in the current patch. I've also made the borders of the battle area slightly visible.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45205026/c05d8f0853875440cbafec4245b6cbd52dfe7ad8.png"][/img][/p][p]
There are also various small improvements and renamings that aren’t worth listing individually.

Thanks for your support![/p]

notes.title: Patch 0.10.2.3 Crafting goods
notes.content:
I've realized that some players are experiencing issues with gold income, so I’ve decided to slightly tweak this aspect of the game. While the main sources of income — buildings and reputation — remain unchanged, the prices of crafted goods have been increased.

Additionally, a new research option and a new tier of trade goods have been added. These new goods are even more valuable but require shards to craft. This change should improve gold income in the early and mid-game, while also diversifying the ways to earn it.

A new tutorial section has also been added to highlight the different methods of making gold.

notes.title: Patch 0.10.2.2 Creature Rework and New Localizations
notes.content:
[p]The Frogizard was one of the first creature models I created, and I was never fully satisfied with its quality. With this patch, I decided to completely rework it into something better. This update fully replaces the old Frogizard model with a new one. Additionally, the Frogizard Mage has received a minor adjustment: it can no longer perform melee attacks and is now purely a ranged caster.


[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45205026/a07cc6adbd5e6706cb040dabf43812f81431b0a8.png"][/img][/p][p][b]
Please note:[/b] If you load a game already in battle, the old model will still be used, and the creature’s animations may appear broken. This is expected and will be resolved once a new battle begins, loading the updated model.[/p][p]Due to translation issues with the names "Frogizard," "Horselike," and similar creatures, we have decided to rename them to more universally understandable terms. They are now known as [b]Demonic Hound[/b], [b]Demonic Horse[/b], and [b]Demonic Insect[/b].[/p][p][b]
Other notable improvements: [/b]Added three new localizations: [b]French, Spanish, and Polish[/b].[/p][p][/p][p]And one last note: after migrating to Unreal Engine 5.6, I discovered that the [b][u]story voiceovers are no longer localized[/u][/b]. I’ve reported this bug to Epic, and once it’s fixed, I’ll restore voice localization. In the meantime, I’ll update the Steam page to reflect the current status. My apologies for the inconvenience.[/p][p]Thank you for your continued support![/p]

notes.title: Patch 0.10.2.0 - Global Map Events
notes.content:
[p][b]Patch 0.10.2.0 - Global Map Events[/b][/p][p]This patch marks the latest major update for the game leading up to its release. I was not entirely satisfied with how global map events were implemented, so I’ve completely reworked that aspect of the game. At this stage, the game [b]includes all the content I intended to have[/b].[/p][p][u][i]I don’t like doing this[/i][/u][i],[/i] but I must humbly ask players: if you enjoy the game, please leave a review on our Steam page. It's incredibly important for the game’s lifecycle and visibility. I apologize for making this request and appreciate any support you can give.[/p][p]Now, I need to focus on marketing and improving the game's visibility—this includes reworking trailers, updating screenshots, refining descriptions, and more.
[/p][h3][b]Patch Changes:[/b][/h3][p]Global map events now trigger less frequently, but they no longer have any disadvantages. While these events still have requirements to pass or fail, failing an event will no longer result in penalties. Events are now divided into [u]seven different types[/u], easily recognizable by their event model. Additionally, better party vehicles offer improved [i][u]reveal complexity attribute[/u], which influence the quality of rewards players can receive. 

[/i]You can learn more about the new event system in the excellent [url="https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3495912573" style="button"]NeverTooOld's guide[/url]. (Please note that it may contain some minor spoilers, but [u]I highly recommend checking it out[/u])[i]
[/i][/p][h3][b]Details:[/b][/h3][h3][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45205026/2997d371acf5ca448e75259f38a49f5d22310b3e.png"][/img][/h3][list][*][p][b]Followers Class Selection[/b]: When starting a new game, players can now pick classes for followers. This change reduces the randomness of party generation slightly.[/p][/*][*][p][b]New Research - Advanced Alchemy[/b]: A new branch of research has been added, along with three new potions and their corresponding recipes.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Crafting Lesser Essence[/b]: Players can now craft a new item called "Lesser Essence," designed to adjust potions in a similar way to how weapons can be upgraded.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Orc & Elf Origins Fix[/b]: The origins for orcs and elves have been corrected. For existing characters, players will need to respec them to apply the changes.[/p][/*][*][p][b]New Ring Slot Items[/b]: Items for the ring slot are now available, improving the proficiency of workers. These items can only be obtained through events.[/p][/*][*][p][b]New Party Buffs[/b]: A new category of party buffs has been introduced. These buffs last up to one week or until the first battle—whichever comes first.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Rebalanced Loot Rewards[/b]: Rewards from global map events have been rebalanced to improve player experience and progression.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45205026/2502fa66929f1ab3439bcb5ce21ef1e0eb62e29c.png"][/img]Thank you for playing and for your continued support![/p][/*][/list]

notes.title: Patch 0.10.1.1: Weight Rebalance
notes.content:
This patch introduces two important updates: a complete rebalance of equipment and the ability to hide headgear.

Previously, there was an issue where a character with 10 strength could not equip full-plate T4 armor without becoming overloaded. This has now been addressed, making it possible to wear such armor. Additionally, other equipment has been rebalanced to reduce weight.

While investing 1-2 additional strength points is still a good choice—as it allows carrying medkits, potions, and is required for multiclassing when using dual weapons—it is no longer mandatory for light armor related subclasses.

notes.title: Patch 0.10.0.9 WIP
notes.content:
The main goal of this update is to show that I am actively working on the game and its improvements. Most of the changes have been gathered from the forums, private messages, or my own findings. There's no point in listing every single change, as they are mostly small but numerous. ))

The demo version is slightly outdated since I haven't had time to update the demo build yet, but I will do so soon.

Thank you all for your feedback, support, and patience as I continue to improve the game!

notes.title: Patch 0.10.0.3 - UE 5.6
notes.content:
This patch uses the latest version of Unreal Engine to date. My internal tests show some FPS improvements. Additionally, it may fix some crashes that occurred previously. I'll review the crash reports to investigate any issues, so please, if you experience a crash, make sure to press "Send and Close" or "Send and Restart."

There are no backward compatibility issues—I’ve tested several saves from the previous version, and they work fine.

This patch also includes some visual improvements and several fixes discussed recently on the forum.

notes.title: Patch 0.10.0.2 Game Completion
notes.content:
[p]This patch is one of the most important updates to the game. It introduces a fully implemented final boss fight, new achievements, and multiple endings, making the game finally complete.[/p][p][/p][p]There are still some minor adjustments that I would like to implement before the full release. One of these is the refactoring of global map events. Additionally, as main development is nearly complete, I now have more time to better balance and improve various aspects of the game. If you have any suggestions or feedback, please feel free to share them with me.[/p][p][/p][p]At this stage, it is difficult to predict exactly when the official full release will occur, but it should be roughly within a month.

[b]Boss fight[/b][/p][p][b]
[/b][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45205026/8857e15d544a01107f2451293ec2a9c728b906ea.png"][/img][/p][p]The final boss fight is designed for a party of 9 people and includes some new mechanics. I won't spoil them here. The [b]fight is challenging[/b] and will require players to demonstrate tactical mastery, along with good gear and effective character builds.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45205026/3b5e339423b6e1901e5eb74cc86ffa3c0a684c6f.png"][/img][/p][p]This patch also includes minor balance adjustments and bug fixes.[/p][p][/p][p]Thank you for your continued support and for playing the game![/p]

notes.title: Patch 0.10.0.0 Too Early
notes.content:
After another sleepless night under rockets and Shaheds, I've decided to release a nearly finished build of the game slightly ahead of schedule :D

This build contains an almost completed version of the game (except for the final voiceovers, minor adjustments to the final map, and a few small details).

I hope to finish up these remaining tasks within the next few days and then make a full-fledged release.

notes.title: Patch 0.9.15.0 Improvements
notes.content:
This patch is primarily aimed at fixing various issues, bugs, and balance adjustments.

[list]
[*] Changed and improved the tutorial section.
[*] Added a mutated version of the Shepherd.
[*] Adjusted mind control mechanics: controlled characters are now more likely to use attack skills.
[*] Increased enemy damage and rebalanced end-game parties to make them more challenging and dangerous.
[*] Various bug fixes
[/list]

notes.title: Patch 0.9.11.0 Story completion
notes.content:
This massive patch introduces extensive new content to the game. The most important update: You can now pick your character's eye color! (All other updates are minor and can safely be skipped... :D )

In all seriousness, the key feature of this patch is the [b]completion of the game's main story[/b]. Apart from the final boss battle (coming soon), the entire storyline can now be experienced fully up to the final encounter.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45205026/b4212644d43354b9b88ad169ebec8824836a9e97.png[/img]

Other notable additions and improvements include:

[list]
[*] Introduced new goals/missions
[*] Introduced numerous new Tier 4 (T4) items such as armors, weapons, rings, and party transports.
[*] Added a brand new tier of dungeons to discover and explore.
[*] Unlocked many new research opportunities.
[*] Included several new crafting recipes.
[*] Implemented a new gameplay mechanic of capturing specific enemies to advance further in the storyline.
[*] Improved the Buildings tab in the fortress menu—now you can click directly on the 3D models of buildings.
[*] The map now displays dungeon locations directly once you've completed the necessary research. It is no longer required to visit the research tab to find dungeon locations.
[*] The Dark Priest weapon now includes a shield. This change better matches the intended off-tank role. Since shields block effects and reduce damage, I'll review whether additional balance adjustments are required for the Dark Priest class or combat overall. To make the shield appear with the existing Dark Priest weapon, you need to re-equip it.
[*] Additionally, this patch addresses numerous small bugs and improves overall game stability.
[/list]

[b]Future Plans[/b]:

Next week, I plan to spend time fixing various issues/improvements reported by the community. After that, I will focus on completing the final boss fight. Once this update is released, the game will advance to version 0.10, indicating that content development is complete. However, I intend to keep the game in Early Access for some time to address balance issues, implement improvements to global events, and enhance overall gameplay quality.

notes.title: Patch 0.9.8.1: Meet New Friends
notes.content:
This patch introduces a substantial amount of new endgame content. I’ve added two new demonic characters—based on their abilities, I’m sure you’ll “love” them. I also expect them to be a bit more powerful than previous enemies (though some say they aren’t so tough… we’ll see).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45205026/9e3369ea6f6c61f3f9f0a93d3d37e883cecfefdf.png[/img]

Reduced the cost of T3 gear, and with the improvements to gathering tools, crafting gear should now be slightly easier. Additionally, all gathering spot buildings now offer a 20% higher gathering rate. I’ve introduced better gathering tools for T2 and T3 as well, allowing faster resource collection in the endgame and giving you more freedom to pursue other activities.

It will no longer be possible to equip identical rings at the same time. On one hand, that makes my life easier; on the other, it adds more complexity to character builds.

Introduced a new research and 8 new T3 buildings. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45205026/fa412f22534ad6586af42adf80d2c1e9130f6940.png[/img]

Adjusted  Demonic Camouflage transport. Now new cool 'ant' will travell with your.

I’m sure I’ve overlooked something—let’s just call it a surprise ))

UPD for 0.9.8.1

While investigating the HP bug, I realized Constitution was too powerful compared to other attributes, so I decided to reduce it from 10 HP per point to 5. At this level, I believe it’s more balanced. This change will affect not only player characters but also some NPCs.

Thank you all for your support!

notes.title: Patch 0.9.5.0 – Outside Buildings
notes.content:
Interaction with allies is one of the most important features in the game. This patch introduces the following mechanics:

 As the world grows, roaming enemy parties become stronger and are more likely to harm guards and villagers. This can lead to settlements being destroyed, causing players to lose any structures they have already built as well as potential trading points. To prevent this, players can close the demonic rift and construct buildings that protect their allies.

This patch adds six new buildings. These buildings can increase both the size and speed of faction guards and improve their equipment. For villagers, players can construct buildings that make them less visible to enemies, which improves their chances of survival.

It's not just virtual changes—the player can see the actual effects of these buildings in the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45205026/950daa9f5c0b8b13ddb97ff83ee2d8649df9b681.png[/img]

Another notable improvement is the overall speed of battles. A new slider has been added to the settings menu to allow players to adjust battle speed according to their preference.

As usual, several bugs have been identified and fixed.

Thank you for your continued support!

notes.title: Patch 0.9.3.3 Crashes
notes.content:
I always try to introduce new and interesting bugs to the game. Unfortunately, the latest one caused the game to crash when starting a new game and doesn't look too interesting for me.

This hotfix should resolve that issue.

My apologies for any inconvenience)

notes.title: Patch 0.9.3.0 – Teleportation Stone
notes.content:
[b]My apologies[/b] for the frequent releases, but I want to deliver important features as soon as possible ))

This patch focuses on improving mid-game party mobility and includes several balance changes:

[list]
[*] Added the [b]Teleportation Stone[/b], which allows the player's party to quickly teleport to either the fortress or the nearest discovered teleport, boosting mobility and survivability.
[*] Some [b]support skills[/b] are now tied to subclasses rather than the base class. Existing characters are unaffected. Certain classes (I won’t say which! ːsteammockingː) were incredibly overpowered when multi-classed; this change should balance them and encourage diversity among subclasses in general.
[*] Houses now offer more [b]living space[/b], making it easier to keep a reserve of companions while wounded members recover.
[*] Increased Medical Kit healing from 25 to 30.
[*] Reduced enemy party sizes by one member.
[*] Soap is now stackable! ːsteamhappyː
[/list]

notes.title: Patch 0.9.2.0 – Sound
notes.content:
This small patch introduces several updates to the game:

• Added different hit sounds depending on the creature or armor type
• The direction of the attack now appears next to the hit percentage for better positioning
• Fixed several known crashes

notes.title: Patch Notes 0.9.1.0 – Story
notes.content:
This patch focuses on moving the story forward. Although it took a bit longer than the originally promised week (not by much!), it adds a significant number of new features. The next missions begin after the current "Influential Allies." To proceed, simply raise your reputation with that faction by at least 1 if you are already friendly. As usual, previous saves may work, but the game may be unbalanced if those saves are very old.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45205026/fe7a052b31ffe8111c3bd2b9b844c42ab2047bfb.png[/img]

Most important changes:

[list]
[*] Added 2 new missions. Although only 2, completing them requires conducting several research tasks, clearing a minimum of 5 dungeons, and more.
[*] Added 10 accessible T2 dungeons to the map. As with T1 dungeons, research is required to unlock them. These T2 dungeons contain new T2 rings and a new type of weapon upgrade: Essences.
[*] Introduced Essences and the required building upgrade. These allow you to improve weapons in different ways, but only once. You may find Essences occasionally in friendly faction stores or T2 dungeons.
[*] Added T2 rings to the game.
[*] Improved global map graphics. Based on testing, this appears to have no impact on performance, but we would appreciate your feedback.
[*] A friendly reputation now not only allows you to build more structures in faction settlements, but also adds items such as Essences or rings to the main town’s store.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45205026/9a04366a6a1c9c39662164a8219a024343f54844.png[/img]

Thank you for your patience!

notes.title: Patch 0.9.0.1: Sight
notes.content:
This patch primarily focuses on improving the game’s visuals and addressing bugs and UI issues. Although it includes some elements for the next stage of game progression (T2 dungeons), they are currently not interactive. I hope to add new rings, research options, and further story progression next week.

The most important change in this patch is the reworked character sight. Character has their own visibility range based on their shape. Tall characters can detect enemies more effectively because they have a better view over covers. This means if you use crouching and covers strategically, you can remain hidden for longer.

We’ve also made a slight UI adjustment to indicate whether player characters are revealed or not. In addition, there is a new feature that shows each character’s actual cone of vision.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45205026/15a2e9d961ac87a913b28df2b9083961f2774593.png[/img]

Other notable changes: 
[list]
[*] Added a world map.
[*] Added T2 dungeons (not yet accessible).
[*] Improved the first battle tutorial mission to explain the sight mechanic and slightly enhanced the UI.
[*] Increased camera movement speed on both the tactical and global maps when using WASD.
[*] Fixed some crashes (please press “Send crash report” — this is the easiest way for us to identify and fix bugs).
[*] Increased the camera’s maximum distance for those who want a broader view of the battlefield.
[/list]

Thank you for all your feedback! It’s helping us make the game better.

notes.title: Patch Notes 0.8.16.0 – Auras
notes.content:
[b]This major patch (0.8.16.0) marks the culmination of core mechanics implementation[/b]. With this milestone, my focus will now shift toward advancing the story and finalizing the game. This patch introduces significant changes across various aspects of the game, with the primary goal of freeing up player time for exploring the world. To enhance character build flexibility and support multiclassing, I've also added new Aura skills.

[b]New Content: Four New Aura Skills[/b]

Four Auras have been introduced to enhance gameplay and provide strategic depth. These skills cost a considerable amount of MP per turn, especially early-game, and provide benefits to allies or debuffs to enemies within range.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45205026/06081fb55d249caf4a768df94c110de0d1ac9fa2.gif[/img]

[u]Aura of Empowerment[/u]
Grants a 15% damage buff to nearby allies.
Consumes 3 MP per turn while active.

[u]Aura of Weakness[/u]
Inflicts a 15% damage debuff on nearby enemies.
Consumes 3 MP per turn while active.

[u]Aura of Void[/u]
Applies a debuff to all nearby enemies, causing them to take unblocked direct damage at the end of their turn.
Consumes 3 MP per turn while active.

[u]Aura of Wind[/u]
Increases the maximum action points of all nearby allies by 2, allowing them to perform a third attack or take other actions during the next turn.

[b]Siege Parties Refactoring[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45205026/b60757d1f948545b6457cf8163bddac92dab0394.png[/img]

Previously, sieges were deactivated due to their complexity and potential to occur too early in the game. To address this, the world growth system has been reworked for greater predictability:
[list]
[*] Siege party progression is now more aligned with the player’s growth path.
[*] New enemy party types have been added, ensuring a better fit with the player's development.
[*] Siege parties now scale their power more gradually, improving pacing and balance.
[*] Visuals for cultist progression and siege beasts have been enhanced for better clarity.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45205026/d201b3b9b2ec08607985d219bde99729c58f580a.png[/img]

[b]Transport Upgrades: Healing on the Move[/b]
Given that resting is a core mechanic for healing wounds, I’ve introduced new transport upgrades to provide healing capabilities while traveling. However, these upgrades come with trade-offs compared to other transport options.

[b]World Changes[/b]
A number of adjustments have been made to resting mechanics and the overall game world:

[list]
[*] Reduced initial building costs: This allows players to construct more starting buildings earlier in the game.
[*] Rift closures extended: Rifts now remain closed for 1.5 months when sealed, granting players more time to protect regions.
[*] Lowered village reputation requirements: Slightly reduced, with an additional slot added at reputation level 16.
[*] Faction gathering spots improved: Increased items (notably alchemy plants) available at faction gathering locations, making them more attractive than spots closer to the player fortress.
[*] Research cost reductions: Several Tier 1 and Tier 2 research costs have been slightly reduced.
[*] Free building slot added to player fortress: Offers players more flexibility in fortress construction.
[*] Dungeon loot tripled: Significantly improved loot retrieved from dungeons.
[*] Balanced enemy strength: Reduced the strength of Rift Protectors and Dungeon Protectors for better scaling.
[*] Companion death loot changes: Equipment from fallen companions can now be retrieved as loot upon victory (excluding dungeon battles, as the primary goal there is escape).
[*] Increased town companions: The number of companions generated in towns has been increased to four.
[*] Bug Fixes and Improvements
[*] Various smaller bug fixes and balance adjustments have been implemented to improve overall gameplay and player experience.
[/list]

Thank you for [u][b]your feedback and patience[/b][/u] as the game continues to evolve! Your input has been invaluable in shaping the mechanics, balance, and overall gameplay experience.

notes.title: Patch 0.8.0.0: Start from Scratch
notes.content:
This is the [b]biggest[/b] update so far. It changes everything related to the global map.

Although I could not migrate to UE 5.5 due to bugs I've found, I used a new package type for the game which should [b]increase performance by up to 50%[/b] compared to previous versions. As a downside of this, I can no longer see errors in the game except for crashes. Please inform me if you find something; I'll create a bugfix thread.

Another important fix is AI changes. I refactored AI-related code and I suppose [b]got rid of AI stucks[/b]. Please let me know if you see this.

The research tree was rebalanced, with new researches added. Researches and crafts are now divided by tiers, and to be able to start new production/research, you now need to have enough research/production points. So, [i]better buildings and skilled workers are required[/i].

The Proficiency Hall was reworked. Now, instead of increasing all proficiencies related to an origin, the player should pick the desired upgrade.

Character origins were reworked to better fit the changes. Now they provide less proficiency attributes but increase the speed of obtaining new proficiencies.

[b]Factions' gathering spots[/b] were improved; they have a better amount of gathered resources but require either reputation with the faction or gathering licenses, which may be bought in factions' settlements.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45205026/843a2bb823eea96e21957590330784c8a7ffdffa.png[/img]

A big rebalance of party [b]vehicles/equipment[/b] was done. New researches were added which allow upgrading existing vehicles. Also, vehicles are now more specialized for hiding/carrying/overall purposes.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45205026/9eac9f80d4e94056bcbd0107a8f95e2a490fb75d.png[/img]

The player's fortress now has 2 additional building slots to allow the construction of all possible buildings (some of them, like the player's own teleport, still in progress).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45205026/2c9dcb5914b0f45703bab937581a8a46a140d356.png[/img]

Almost all buildings now have upgrades or better versions for mid-game (research required). The first tier of buildings is split into basic and upgraded versions to construct different buildings much easier, but to have the full power of them, they need to be upgraded.

Settlement slots now require different reputation with the faction to allow construction.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45205026/c72b1466220269db192a1d82a8fb6756ca306016.png[/img]

Wages were reduced, but overall income from gold was reduced as well. Now [b]money management should be more important[/b] than before.

Slowed down characters' regeneration on the map. Hospitals are now more important than before.

New items and crafts have been added.

Overall, all global map gameplay should be smoother but more [b]challenging[/b].

[b]Thank you, and waiting for your feedback! :)[/b]

notes.title: Announcement of Patch 0.8.0.0
notes.content:
Merry Christmas and Happy New Year! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45205026/8e43b7fb99293fb5707e38bd81feec9df2df6aba.png[/img]

[b]First of all, I would like to thank the community. Your effort and suggestions help me to make the game better![/b]

Next, I would like to share some important upcoming updates.

For those who don't want a long read, here's a quick summary:

[list]
[*] There will not be a patch this week, but the next one in the new year will have significant improvements.
[*] [strike]I'm planning to migrate to UE 5.5; this will [b]break save compatibility[/b].[/strike]
[*] New packaging of the game will be used, which will increase [b]performance by up to 50%[/b].
[*] [b]Full rebalance[/b] for crafting recipes and constructions.
[*] [b]Rework[/b] of research and craft system.
[/list]

Now, let's proceed with a more detailed read and explanations.

[strike]Migrating to Unreal Engine 5.5 may fix some engine-related crashes and improve game performance. Additionally, 5.5 has significant improvements in the lighting system, which will allow me to attempt to improve the visual aspect of the game. However, a downside is that each UE version change breaks save compatibility. Also, the new version may introduce new bugs, but let's believe in the better :)[/strike]
UPD: I've tested the migrated version. It's unplayable... Maybe later I'll give migrating another try, but not now...

UE has several "modes" to package the game for play. The current development mode is good for testing and finding bugs, but lacks performance. For the next update, I'll use the shipped build. Tests on my PC show a 50% improvement in FPS between them. It's significant, so I'll sacrifice testing options to make the game more performant.

By analyzing crashes and saved games sent to me by players, I've realized that the fortress management aspect isn't as critical as I had hoped. There's a noticeable lack of strategy in many constructions. Moreover, as the game allows for a variety of strategies, it leads to the neglect of some important buildings and researches. Consequently, other tier researches and crafts, which aren't ignored, end up requiring an excessive amount of time because they are often handled by one or two low-level scientists or craftsmen.

So, the most important change in the next patch will be a strict separation of researches and recipes into tiers and introducing a required threshold. Research/craft will not be able to start without proper buildings/proficient workers. Players have flexibility in how to achieve this. Also, once the research/craft has started, it will not require the threshold for proceeding, but lowering research/production points will lead to an increased amount of time (up to infinity :) )

This change should also make game progression smoother, without overpowering player characters too early.

I will introduce new resources. Existing recipes will be rebalanced, and new researches and building upgrades will be added.

In the nearest plans, there are mutations for starting creatures, which will improve their attributes for the mid-game. It will not be just hidden changes in numbers, but visual adjustments as well. However, I don't know if I could do it in the next update (most probably not).

Thank you all!

notes.title: Patch 0.7.4.0 Rings
notes.content:
The main goal of this patch is to introduce rings into the game. Rings or recipes for crafting rings can be found in dungeons (see previous patch). Dungeons are located across faction lands and need to be discovered. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45205026/768823ecc31721d88502f7e304134f3bcf9ce6cd.png[/img]

Dungeons are now separated by faction and contain faction-specific lists of recipes/rings that can be found inside. This means there is no way to find all possible recipes/rings in a single dungeon. Dungeons close to the player's fortress contain only [b]one recipe/item inside a chest[/b], but other dungeons [b]contain two recipes/items[/b]. To be able to craft a ring, the player must find the recipe, research it, and then craft it.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45205026/b51ded9cbe5d990db6d8189061ace41c06d51ab1.png[/img]

[b]Building upgrades[/b] are introduced in this game update. A new research has been added, and after completing it, players can upgrade certain buildings.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45205026/d9d0556f65cac1d8caff78c189e2478892ee06eb.png[/img]

Another important change is the [b]workers rebalance[/b]. Currently, buildings may contain both required and optional working slots. A building will not work if any of its required slots are empty, but these slots provide full points to the building's production. Optional slots don't affect whether the building operates, but they do provide only [b]half of the production points[/b]. For example, if a building has 1 required and 1 optional slot and workers with 1 production point each are assigned, this building will produce 1.5 points. However, for a building with 2 required slots, production will be 2 points.

List of changes:

[list]
[*] Added rings, ring recipes, and corresponding research
[*] Added new complex materials required for crafting rings
[*] Rebalanced research: Ancient equipment previously appeared in the game too early. Now, research requires trained workers. There are two ways to train a worker: the Proficiency Hall building and increasing main attributes.
[*] Added building upgrades and new research for that
[*] Reduced the cost of the laboratory and workshop and added upgrades to them
[*] [b]Added detailed info about expenses and income for gold when hovering in the global map UI[/b]

Currently, there are 14 dungeons placed throughout the world, generally in the territories of factions and near the player's fortress. They are hidden until the player discovers them. The dungeons are designed for a prepared party, ideally consisting of 6 well-equipped members.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45205026/2ab2d6a8f4c308bb7f4b494b44c72b5779a9a3f3.gif[/img]

To be able to enter a dungeon, you need to complete the required research first.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45205026/d18811392677a34f98737deb253b5644ff264db9.png[/img]

Inside the dungeon, you need to find a hidden chest, open it, take the recipe, and escape. Be cautious, as enemies will arrive over time.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45205026/7da9b51422dbc3f4eed1f00868f2e74f63f75371.png[/img]

After the battle, the recipe will be in your party's inventory or the inventory of the character who picked it up (if the party inventory was full).

You need to investigate the recipe if it's unidentified, or sell it if you already know that recipe. Afterward, you will be able to craft items. In the current patch, only resource recipes are available. The patch has reduced the amount of resources needed for crafting but slightly increased the crafting duration.

You will be able to visit the same dungeon only after a 30-day delay.

Later, rings, amulets, and their recipes will also be found inside.

Thank you!

notes.title: Patch 0.7.0.0 - Let War Begin and Dungeons
notes.content:
This patch introduces a huge number of changes but [b]unfortunately breaks backward compatibility[/b] with old saves. Although old saves may work and can be loaded, [u]there is no way to adjust[/u] the existing game to the new setup, and older games will be unbalanced.

I aim to make combat more dynamic and add more build variety to battles. Therefore, I increased the number of units in battle. Players now start with a party of [b]5 people instead of 3[/b], and the maximum party size is now 8-9 people. Accordingly, all opposing parties have been increased as well.

Starting with this patch, I will work on [b]new crafting recipes[/b] (including rings and amulets) which can be found in dungeons. To support this, a completely new map generator for Dungeons has been created. In this patch, dungeons cannot be found in the main game but can be encountered in roguelike mode. Currently, they contain random loot.

[b]I would like to ask you to share your thoughts about the new battle balance )[/b]

The list of noticeable changes made:
[list]

[*]Global game rebalance: The starting party is now 5 people, and the rest of the world is scaled up as well.
[*]New map type introduced - Dungeons: A new battle goal, hide treasures and escape, has been introduced. These dungeons use a completely different map generator and will be the main source of unique items like recipes for rings and amulets.
[*]War! Now there are pairs of factions at war with each other. A new type of party, Invaders, has been introduced, whose goal is to inflict as much damage to their hostile faction as possible.
[*]Gaining and losing reputation: Gaining reputation with one faction will lead to a loss of reputation with its hostile faction.
[*]Faction lands: Each faction now has its own specific territory. Killing enemies of a faction on its lands will increase your reputation with that faction, as well as liberating gathering spots belonging to the faction.
[*]Faction dynamics: Since it’s not possible to be friendly with all factions (due to losing reputation with the opposing faction), you may need to decide who should survive. Kill villagers, steal their goods, but be cautious of the guards...
[*]Reworked idea of followers: Only the main character now doesn't require wages. All starting companions will have no wages only for the first week of the game. As the initial tavern quest covers these expenses, it’s not an issue. However, this will lead to members possibly leaving if not paid, except for the main character (previously, the main character and starting companions could not leave due to the absence of wages).
[*]Bug fixes

[/list]
Thank you for your continued interest in the game. I hope you enjoy the new features and changes in this patch! I am looking forward to your feedback regarding the new features.

notes.title: Patch 0.6.3.0 Tier 3 weapons, trading
notes.content:
This major content update focuses on starting balance, new tier weapon research and crafting queue, and trading.
[list]

[*]Greatly reduced the cost of buildings but slightly increased the time required to build them. The goal is to allow players to construct more starting buildings to better manage their exact needs.
[*]In the previous implementation, any companion could speed up the building process, but Artisans did it better. Now, any companion can increase building speed, but the best speed-up is given by assigning the same worker type as the building. For example, an Artisan is better for building a workshop, but a Scientist is better for a laboratory, and a Worker is best for a farm.
[*]The Proficiency Hall has been slightly adjusted to remove deviation in companion professions. Now, companions may increase their profession up to a maximum of 1 (base) + 1 (5 x profession upgrades) + 1 (from attributes) = 3.
[*]Increased the duration for some researches to balance the progress of research with fortress buildings.
[*]A new grade of weapons has been added to the main game, which includes related research, new items, and recipes. These are designed with the assumption that a library has at least 2 scientists assigned.
[*]Reduced the time required to craft trading goods.
[*]Researches are now sorted by complexity. This can serve as a small tip to understand how complex a research topic is. Detailed info on research now shows speed-ups for the selected research.
[*]Added a dynamic Trading Tax: if a settlement already has certain goods, it buys them for up to 50% less, offering less money for these items. If a settlement has items for too long, it may sell them for up to 50% less.
[*]Reduced the basic trading extra charge from x3 to x2. Reputation now affects settlement prices.
[*]Most trading inventories finally support double-click and Shift + double-click to transfer items, in addition to drag-and-drop.
[*]Added new gathering spots nearby settlements. These are restricted, and collecting from them requires a friendly reputation with the owning faction. Gathering without the necessary reputation leads to a loss in reputation with the owning faction.
[*]Factions now specialize in specific resources (3 for each faction), so they always have their specialized resources available for trade and never miss them.

[/list]

notes.title: Patch Notes 0.6.2.0
notes.content:
This patch brings several new features to the game. As mentioned in the previous patch, I have spent time creating a [b]"roguelike" mode[/b]. This mode focuses solely on battles, party management, and trade—excluding research, crafting, exploration, gathering, and other activities that some players might not enjoy. The main purpose of this mode is to test different builds, identify weaknesses, and find overpowered elements. This mode, along with the main game, may be improved based on your feedback. Please share your thoughts if you are interested, and I'll see what can be done.

Here’s what has been added:
[list]
[*] Added roguelike mode.
[*] Completely refactored AoE zones and related spells like Fire Wall.
[*] Holding the Alt key now also displays AoE zones' geometry, as effects may sometimes appear slightly outside of the actual collision area.
[*] Slightly decreased NPC damage.
[*] Rebalanced player armor to make different types more distinct. Increased indirect damage reduction for light armor.
[*] Improved AI to be slightly smarter.
[*] Added autosave at the start of the player's turn in battles.
[*] Adjusted all existing maps and added a new demonic location, with the goal of providing more cover options on maps.
[*] Dark Priest has been moved to an off-tank/tank role. It can now use heavy armor and has a passive ability for Fright to taunt enemies. Extended Shadow Protection to 2 turns.
[*] Resolved minor issues that were found.
[/list]
As character progression advances, I plan to return to global map improvements. Currently, new weapons are in progress, and I would also like to add recipes and rings.

As usual, I'm eagerly awaiting your feedback, especially regarding the complexity of fights. Thank you for your support!

notes.title: Path notes 0.6.1.0
notes.content:
Before diving into the patch details, a quick heads-up: tomorrow, I plan to slightly increase the game's price.

Now, onto the patch. This substantial update brings numerous improvements, with a primary focus on character progression. I'll provide a list of added perks at the end. Existing save games should remain compatible.

Here's a brief overview of the patch update:
[list]
[*] Introduced over 40+ new passive perks aimed at enhancing characters' roles. Each character's skill now features 1-2 upgrades. These upgrades extend beyond mere percentage increases, potentially altering skill behavior.

[*] Added a new building that allows character respec. Characters must have no equipped items to be eligible for respec. Currently, the building costs 50, and respec takes 1 hour per character level. Both the cost and respec time are subject to increase before the full release. This feature requires Basic Constructions research.

[*] Redesigned the player's fortress model for improved aesthetics.

[*] Adjusted character progression to lend more significance to multiclassing (e.g., the 2nd level now grants both 1 skill point and 1 feature point). This change won't apply automatically to existing characters; they will need to be respecced (refer to the point above).

[*] Implemented minor bug fixes uncovered during development.

[*] Given the increased complexity and variety of builds, I'm considering introducing a new rogue-like mode focused solely on consecutive fights, eliminating building and exploration aspects. This mode would facilitate quicker testing of different builds in combat, helping identify overpowered and underperforming characters. It's currently my top priority for the near future. I'd greatly appreciate any suggestions for this mode since rogue-likes are not my forte, and I lack expertise in that area :)
[/list]

List of added perks and buffs/debuffs:

QuickFireball: Costs 2 MP, but requires 1 AP less, and boasts a 30% AoE range.
FireWallNoHarm: Fire wall no longer harms allies or its caster.
FireballNonAoE: Fireball now transforms into a directional projectile, forfeiting its AoE damage in favor of a 10% damage increase.
FirewallWithBurning: The size of Fire Wall has been reduced by 30%, but it now inflicts burning on targets, dealing 50% of the base damage over 2 turns.
BurningDirectSource: Burns and applies damage over time, taking effect at the end of each turn.
BurningAoESource: Burns and applies damage over time, taking effect at the end of each turn.
BitingFrostbolt: Increases damage by 30% if the target is already afflicted by the FrostBite or Chill debuff.
ContagiousFrostbolt: The Frostbolt now costs 1 MP, but chill effect of Frostbolt now become an aura that affects only allies and the caster, within a range of 3m.
WildArcaneCold: Arcane Cold now costs an additional 2 MP, has a usage limit of 1 per turn, and requires no ammo.
BlindingArcaneCold: Arcane Cold additionally applies Blinding cold effect, which interrupts targets' watch if active.
GenerousMagicShield: Additionally increases current and max shield of allies in protected area.
ShieldAddition: Increases current and max shield for 1 turn. Amount scaled by Intelligence.
ProtectiveTeleport: After teleporting, applies the Inner Core buff, which increases shield regeneration.
InnerCore: Increases shield regeneration by 4 (scaled by Constitution) for 1 turn.
MagicVulnerability: Applies a vulnerability to the target, increasing incoming magic damage.
PhysicVulnerability: Applies a vulnerability to the target, increasing incoming physic damage.
VulnerableInflictWound: Additionally applies Magic vulnerability to the target.
PowerfulInflictWound: Now applies immediate damage upon hitting, in addition to damage over time, but costs 1 MP additionally.
HarmonyMaceHit: Reduces threat by 1 upon a successful hit. Increases damage of Mace Hit by 10%.
DecreaseThreat: Decreases thread by 1.
RestorativeMaceHit: Restores 5% of the owner's HP on a successful hit against targets with any debuff. Increases the damage of Mace Hit by 15% against targets with debuffs.
VampiricTouch: Restores 5% HP on hit, if target has Inflict wounds debuff.
ExtensiveFright: Upon use, any Damage Over Time (DoT) applied to the target will instantly take effect, but costs 1 MP additionally.
DoTForceTrigger: Any Damage Over Time (DoT) applied to the target will instantly take effect.
GenerousSupport: Applies effect to all nearby allies around target. Range is 250.
ProtectiveHeal: Has 10% increased effect and usage radius, also grants Careful step buff on target.
GreatHeal: Heal become AoE around caster, which heals all targets in range.
FocusedStarlight: Starlight now also inflicts immediate damage in addition to DoT, but costs 1 MP and 1 ammo additionally.
WildStarlight: On successful hit Starlight heals nearest to target ally. Amount of heal is scaled by Perception.
WildStarlightOnOwner: this text anyway should nobody to see.
ProtectiveHit: Increased damage by 10%. Successful hit grants Protection buff.
Protection: Increases all armor types except indirect by 1 per stack.
ProvocatingHit: Increases damage by 10% and applies Taunt on the target upon hitting.
ThriftyHinderingBlow: Hindering Blow costs 1 MP less and has 10% increased damage.
WeakeningHinderingBlow: Additionally applies Weakness to the target reducing damage.
Weakness: Reduces damage by 15%.
VulnerableTwoHandedAttack: Two handed attack also applies Physical vulnerability on hit.
BleedingTwoHandedAttack: Two handed attack also applies Bleeding on hit.
RecklessTwoHandedSpin: If the berserk is afflicted with any debuff, Two-Handed Spin deals an additional 25% damage.
MadTwoHandedSpin: Two-Handed Spin has its damage increased by 5% for each hostile character within range.
PreparedTaunt: Taunt now inflicts 5 direct damage (increased by Dexterity) and interrupts watch on the target.
DuelChallenge: Inflicts 5 direct damage (increased by Strength) and interrupts watch on the target.
ReplenishDash: Replenish Dash instantly restores 5 HP to us (scaled by Dexterity).
ReplenishDashEffect: Instantly restores 5 HP to us (scaled by Dexterity).
Slow: Slow increases the AP cost of each skill usage by 1.
CripplingSpearHit: Spear Hit inflicts 10% more damage and applies Slow on the target.
BrotherhoodSpearHit: Deals 5% more damage for each ally within a 250 range.
PreparedSpearThrowing: Reduces cost by 1 AP and 1 MP, deals +10% damage, but limited to 1 usage per turn.
PoisonedSpearThrowing: Spear throwing now inflicts Poison on the target upon hitting.
DoubleBowShot: Fires an additional arrow with decreased precision, reduces damage by 10%, and costs an additional 1 MP.
DistantBowShot: Deals an additional 15% damage to targets farther than 700.
QuickPoisonArrow: Inflicts 10% more damage and costs 1 AP less but deals 10 direct damage to the user upon use (reduced by Constitution).
Bluntness: Instantly inflicts 10 direct damage. May be reduced by constitution.
EmpoweredPoisonArrow: If under the effect of any buff, inflicts 15% more damage.
TelepathicAnimalSight: Animal Sight now instantly reveals one random hidden enemy, but at the cost of an additional 1 AP and 1 MP.
AnimalHelp: Instantly reveals one random hidden enemy.
ResilientCopyReplacer: Copy now possesses half of the owner's health, allowing it to sustain more damage before disappearing.

notes.title: Path notes 0.6.0.0
notes.content:
As previously mentioned, [b]old saves will no longer be compatible[/b]. The new patch requires starting a new game. Old saves can be [u]manually[/u] deleted from the folder [i]{pathToSteam}\SteamLibrary\steamapps\common\ShardsOfRealm\Tactical\Saved\SaveGames[/i]. With the latest release version of Unreal Engine now in use, I recommend updating your video card drivers.

In addition to migrating to a new version of Unreal Engine, this patch includes many enhancements and new content. I've expanded our mid-game offerings, introducing new maps, potions, activities, and modes of transport. It's challenging to estimate the additional playtime provided, but I anticipate that acquiring the latest transport and all available equipment could extend gameplay by around 5-6 hours.
[list]
[*] New Battle Activity: Rifts: As you explore the world, you may encounter open rifts. Attempting to close them will yield rare mid-game resources, though be prepared for battles significantly tougher than those usually encountered in the world.

[*] Demonic Creatures: After completing mid-game research, you'll have the ability to tame demonic creatures, currently usable for 5-person transport. I'm considering further uses for these creatures in construction and am open to suggestions on the Steam forum.

[*] Basic Alchemy Research: Now enables the crafting of four new potions.

[*] 5-Person Transport: Newly added transport requires completing a research chain to craft.

[*] Public Teleports Rework: Teleports have been reworked to allow for teleportation to specific chosen destinations, moving away from the previous chain-teleport system.

[*] Hidden Transport Parameter: Added a hidden parameter to transport that aids in revealing hidden POIs like rifts.

[*] Flexible Battle Initiation: Many battles at POIs can now be postponed, allowing you to choose when to engage (day/night) and to prepare for battle (save the game, equip items).

[*] New Building Requirements: Introduced new requirements for constructing buildings outside, paving the way for later construction of faction-unique buildings in settlements.

[*] Protector’s Shield Bash Adjustment: Now decreases the target's precision.

[*] Access to Storage from Members Tab: Players can now access Storage inventory directly from the Members tab.

[*] Weapon Damage Increase: The damage of 1st-tier weapons has been increased by 10%, making the difference between starting and crafted weapons 20%.

[*] Berserk Watch Fix: Addressed an issue with the berserk watch.

[*] Minor Fixes: Implemented numerous other small fixes and adjustments.
[/list]
Thank you for your continued support. I look forward to hearing your feedback and suggestions on the Steam forum.

notes.title: Patch notes 0.5.2.0
notes.content:
First of all, I would like to thank Roberto for providing saves, which helped me to examine the game from a user's perspective and identify numerous issues that would have been difficult for me to find otherwise.

The new patch brings balance changes as well as stability improvements. I tried my best to ensure existing saves would remain compatible, but due to significant core changes, I cannot be certain. Most likely, they should work (tested on Roberto's saves). Below is a list of the most important changes:

[list]
[*] Reversed keys for movement and rotation. Now, the RMB is used for movement and the LMB for rotation and selecting characters. This helps to avoid unnecessary movement.
[*] Added durability. It now applies to gathering tools and partially to equipment. Equipment loses durability, but it currently has no impact; this will be addressed in the upcoming patch.
[*] Added the Left Alt key action to highlight all visible characters in battle.
[*] Decreased the default world growth speed. Unfortunately, I could not adjust this for existing saves, and thus the world growth will be reset to 1 for those saves.
[*] Removed accidentally added crafting recipes; they can now be acquired through the intended research, as originally designed.
[*] Reduced the number of enemies on the map, dependent on each world level.
[*] Settlements now refresh their gold over time, depending on the number of living dwellers.
[*] 'Cargo horse' vehicle now increased party size by 1 to 4
[*] Tutorial creatures: reduced amount of armor
[*] Reduced the amount of gold required to build a Hospital, as it's a highly necessary building at lower levels.
[*] Various internal fixes which are not visible to players.
[/list]

notes.title: Shards of Realm: Early Access Update
notes.content:
Dear Adventurers,

I hope this message finds you all well and excited for your adventures in "Shards of Realm." I want to share an important update with you today regarding our journey together.

Recently "Shards of Realm" was mistakenly released as a full version instead of its intended Early Access status. I'm relieved and pleased to inform you that this issue has now been resolved with the help of Steam. "Shards of Realm" is officially in Early Access, as originally planned.

I deeply appreciate your understanding and patience while I navigated this challenge. Your support means the world to me, and your feedback during this time has been both invaluable and heartening.

What This Means Moving Forward:

Ongoing Development: "Shards of Realm" is a labor of love and a work in progress. As a solo developer, I'm fully committed to expanding and enriching this world, relying heavily on your feedback and experiences to guide its growth.

Your Voice Matters: Now, more than ever, your insights, suggestions, and critiques are crucial. "Shards of Realm" is our shared adventure, and I'm here to listen and adapt, making our journey together truly magical.

The Adventure Continues: With Early Access, we’re embarking on an exciting phase of development. There's a lot I plan to add to "Shards of Realm," and I can't wait to share these updates with you.

For anyone who purchased the game thinking it was in its final state, I’m genuinely sorry for any confusion this has caused. I stand by Steam’s refund policy if you feel that the current version isn’t what you were expecting.
